title: Token Slot Jitter Attribution and KV-prefetch Impact Study
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Background: Production traces and per-request metrics show intermittent 'slot jitter' — variability in per-token emission timing that is not explained by sequence length or model compute alone. Hypothesis: a combination of KV-prefetch timing, prefetch misses, and background GC/host noise creates slot-level spikes which get charged to tokens inconsistently. This ticket scopes an instrumentation and analysis experiment to attribute jitter to concrete causes (prefix-store prefetch, cache hit/miss, kernel scheduling delay, and IO stalls).

Goals:
- Produce per-token 'slot delta' metrics correlated with KV-prefetch events and kernel scheduling markers.
- Build a lightweight causal model that attributes each significant token latency spike to one or more root causes (prefetch miss, cache eviction, IO wait, scheduling).
- Surface aggregated dashboards and a daily report to quantify the billing / SLO impact of jitter and recommend mitigation knobs (prefetch window tuning, eager cache warming, scheduling constraints).

Out of scope: Instrumenting model internals unrelated to serving runtime (e.g., optimizer internals) and full rework of scheduler (this ticket focuses on observation and short-term mitigations).
acceptance_criteria: Library-level trace hook added to serving runtime that emits a KV-prefetch span with prefetch_id and keys_requested
Per-token span includes slot_start, slot_end, kv_prefetch_id (if any), cache_hit boolean, and scheduling_marker tags
Daily dashboard shows top-3 root causes for >95th percentile token slot latency and a projected monthly billing delta
Low-overhead sampling: adds <1.5% p99 tail to production inference latencies in canary region under synthetic load
Playbook entry created with mitigation suggestions and a follow-up ENG ticket for remediation work
tasks: Design trace schema and field names (span names, tag keys) and review with observability team
Add lightweight KV-prefetch spans to runtime prefetch path (unique prefetch_id)
Annotate token emission spans with kv_prefetch_id and cache_hit flag
Implement a sampling config that prioritizes capturing high-latency requests and warm-start sequences
Build a trace aggregator job that joins token spans and prefetch spans to compute attribution scores
Create Grafana dashboards: token-slot-latency heatmap, attribution breakdown, billing impact summary
Run canary across eu-west-1 and us-west-2 with synthetic workloads and collect telemetry
Draft mitigation playbook and present findings to SRE and Runtime teams
design_notes: Correlation: use prefetch_id (UUID) propagated in request context so token spans can reference prefetch events
Sampling policy: deterministic sampling for requests with slot delta > 2x expected median, plus reservoir sampling for coverage
Payload size considerations: avoid embedding large key lists in spans; emit key_count and hashed key-fingerprint instead
Privacy: do not log user prompt contents in spans; keep traces keyed by request_id only
Overhead budget: aim for <= 25 bytes per sampled span when compressed; measure CPU overhead in canary
telemetry_schema: metric: token.slot_latency_ms (histogram tags: model, region, route, cache_hit:true|false)
metric: kv.prefetch_latency_ms (histogram tags: model, region, prefetch_window_ms)
trace span: runtime.prefetch {prefetch_id, keys_requested_count, key_fingerprint, start_ts, end_ts}
trace span: runtime.token_emit {request_id, token_index, slot_start_ts, slot_end_ts, kv_prefetch_id}
log event: slot_jitter_alert {request_id, token_index, observed_latency_ms, attribution_tags}
testing_plan: Unit tests for prefetch span creation and propagation in runtime code paths
Integration test that simulates prefetch miss/hit and asserts token spans reference prefetch_id
Load test in canary region with synthetic prompts to measure instrumentation overhead and false-positive rate
A/B comparison: measure p95/p99 tail with instrumentation enabled vs disabled under identical load
rollout_plan: Enable in canary region for 48 hours and run synthetic benchmark harness
If canary metrics OK (overhead <1.5% p99 delta and data quality acceptable), enable on 10% of traffic in us-west-2
Increase to 50% after 72 hrs, then to 100% if no regressions and storage cost within budget
